findings.issue: SetupPackageReader.Inspect returns a live SetupPackage even when the check list failed (OtherDevice, Older, Revoked, a failed Organisation item after the signature held). SetupPackage.Read/ReadLogo/ExtractTo are not gated on Checks.IsAcceptable, so a W03 screen that shows the detail list and then reads an entry would decrypt setup.json (deviceSeed + officeKey) out of a file this installation has just refused. Only SetupInspection.Require()/EnsureAcceptable() gate it, and those are opt-in.
findings.fix: In SetupPackage.Read(string) and SetupPackage.ExtractTo(string), call Checks.EnsureAcceptable() as the first statement (after ObjectDisposedException.ThrowIf) so the payload can only be taken out of a file that passed every required item; if W03 needs to preview a logo from a rejected file, expose that as an explicitly named second method rather than as the default path.

findings.issue: SetupExpectations.StagingDirectory defaults to null, which ContainerWriter.CreateStagingFile turns into Path.GetTempPath(). ContainerReader.DecryptPayload writes the whole decrypted inner zip there, so on a first run the cleartext setup.json - deviceSeed and officeKey included - is written to %TEMP% on disk. FileOptions.DeleteOnClose and the per-user ACL limit the exposure, but the bytes do reach a folder the product does not control. The same applies to SetupWriteRequest.StagingDirectory on the administration-tool side.
findings.fix: Either make StagingDirectory required for the setup reader/writer (throw CryptoException(Corrupt) in SetupPackageReader.Validate and SetupPackageWriter.Prepare when it is null or empty), or record in the B1 acceptance notes that W02 must pass the product's own protected folder; document whichever is chosen in the XML doc of SetupExpectations.StagingDirectory.

findings.issue: Role vocabulary disagrees between the governing documents: DATA-MODEL.md line 31 gives installation.role as director/secretary/custodian, while ARCHITECTURE.md line 81 (and therefore SetupRoles) gives manager|secretary|custodian. The builder correctly followed ARCHITECTURE and the package specification, but B1 will write SetupRoles.Manager into a column the data model says holds 'director'.
findings.fix: Supervisor decision, not a code change here: reconcile docs/build/DATA-MODEL.md line 31 with docs/build/ARCHITECTURE.md line 81 on one of the two spellings before B1 maps setup.json into the installation row; if 'director' wins, SetupRoles.Manager is renamed then and only then.

findings.issue: DeviceKind.Org, DeviceCertificate.IssueOrgRoot, the 'organisation' role constant, the empty-OfficeId shape rule and the 'an Org producer may sign only a Setup container' rule are a new trust-model decision that exists only in code and XML docs. ARCHITECTURE.md sections 3 and 4 still describe certificates as (org, office, deviceId, ...) issued by the organisation key, with no root-certificate concept.
findings.fix: Supervisor to record the decision in ARCHITECTURE.md section 3 (root certificate: DeviceId = IssuerId = OrgId, OfficeId empty, role 'organisation', self-signed as proof of possession) and section 4 (an Org producer may produce only a ContainerKind.Setup container, enforced on both the write and the read side). The builder could not edit docs/.

findings.issue: SetupWriteRequest.Kdf is public and unclamped downward: Argon2Params.Validate only enforces 32 MB / 1 iteration / 1 lane, so the administration tool can ship a production setup file at a quarter of the product's stated cost (64 MB / 3 / 2). The XML doc says the weak path exists for the test suite, but nothing enforces that.
findings.fix: In SetupPackageWriter.BuildRequest, clamp the effective parameters upward to Argon2Params.CreateDefault() unless a deliberate internal test hook is used - e.g. keep Kdf but raise MemoryKb/Iterations/Parallelism to at least DefaultMemoryKb/DefaultIterations/DefaultParallelism, or mark the property internal and let the test assembly reach it through the existing InternalsVisibleTo.

findings.issue: SetupPackage.Read caches every decrypted entry in _read for the life of the package, so a multi-megabyte guide.pdf stays in managed memory until Dispose. This is the builder's own open issue 4 and is a memory-pressure point for W03, which may read the logo, the guide and the template in one session.
findings.fix: Either drop the cache for the three optional entries and let the caller stream them (add ReadTo(string entryName, Stream destination) that forwards to ContainerReader without buffering), or cache only entries below a stated size threshold; document whichever is chosen on SetupPackage.Read.

findings.issue: A setup file whose organisation root certificate carries an IssuedAt more than a day ahead of the clock fails CertificateChain with ErrorCode.Expired, and Examine routes every non-Tampered chain error to SetupCheckItem.Signature. W03 would then say the signature is wrong when the real fault is a date, and Expired is not one of the codes the specification's reader vocabulary names.
findings.fix: In SetupPackageReader.Examine, treat chainError == ErrorCode.Expired the way the container-open path already treats it: record checks.Ok(SetupCheckItem.Signature) and checks.Failed(SetupCheckItem.Package, ErrorCode.FutureDate) instead of failing the Signature item, so the whole format reports one code for one cause.

findings.issue: ContainerReader.Open reads manifest.json in full through ReadAll before the Ed25519 signature is checked, with no cap on the inflated size. A crafted container whose manifest.json is a deflate bomb exhausts memory on a machine that is merely inspecting an untrusted setup file - the same threat model the new Argon2 ceiling was added for. Pre-existing and outside the Setup folder, so noted rather than charged to this package.
findings.fix: Give ReadAll an explicit limit (for example 1 MB for manifest.json and signature.bin, which are tiny by construction) and throw CryptoException(ErrorCode.Corrupt) as soon as it is passed, mirroring CopyWithLimit on the payload side.

notes:
COMMANDS. Ran exactly `dotnet build src/Wakeel.Crypto` then `dotnet test tests/Wakeel.Crypto.Tests` from D:\AI\Administration2. Build: Build succeeded, 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s) with TreatWarningsAsErrors=true. Tests: Failed 0, Passed 212, Skipped 0, Total 212, 4 s - the 176-test baseline plus 36 new cases, nothing regressed. I modified no file and ran no git command beyond read-only status/diff. This package touches no Desktop/UI/Design code, so the host-launch rule does not apply.

SCOPE AND HYGIENE. git status shows Wakeel.Crypto changes confined to Setup/ (new), Certificates/DeviceCertificate.cs, Certificates/CertificateChain.cs, Containers/{ContainerReader,ContainerWriter,ContainerEntrySource}.cs, CryptoException.cs and Primitives/Argon2Params.cs, plus the three test files. Wakeel.Crypto.csproj is untouched and still references only NSec.Cryptography and Konscious.Security.Cryptography.Argon2, both centrally pinned - no NuGet package was added. Directory.Build.props, Directory.Packages.props, Wakeel.slnx and docs/ are clean in the working tree. The other dirty paths (Wakeel.UI deletions, Wakeel.Design, Wakeel.Core, Wakeel.Desktop, the UI tests) belong to the concurrent B0.5 design-system and Core packages, not to this one. The three ErrorCode members are appended after Corrupt, so no existing ordinal shifts.

SPEC ITEM BY ITEM - all six are implemented.
(1) Every field ARCHITECTURE section 4 names is present with the right type and the right bound: SetupOrg (id, name, signingPub, x25519Pub, cycleStartDay 1-28 enforced against SetupOrg.Min/MaxCycleStartDay, numberingFormat), SetupUnit (id, parentId, level 1-4, name, headTitle, headName, officeCode), SetupOffice, SetupDevice (id, deviceNo 1-9, role, syncScope, certificate), DeviceSeeds, SetupEmployee (name, employeeNo 1-9, jobTitle), officeKey (32 bytes, checked), RevocationList?, SetupIncludes. Serialised through CanonicalJson as setup.json; the optional entries carry exactly the three specified names. The_description_carries_exactly_the_fields_the_format_names pins the wire names and the canonical ordering.
(2) SetupPackageWriter.Write exists for both a path and a stream, takes the content, the optional stream factories, the package password, the organisation DeviceIdentity and a TimeProvider, and produces a ContainerKind.Setup / PayloadMode.Password container. The org-root signer question is answered coherently: IssueOrgRoot builds a self-signed certificate with DeviceId = IssuerId = OrgId and an empty OfficeId, CertificateChain gained an Org case that requires those identities, requires the certificate's Ed25519 key to BE the key the verifier holds (so a pinned-key mismatch surfaces as Tampered) and requires a valid self-signature as proof of possession, and ValidateShape now keys the OfficeId rule off the kind so a root can never be read as a device of an office. ContainerWriter.Validate and ContainerReader.Open both refuse an Org producer on any kind but Setup, closing the obvious abuse of the root key as a second identity inside an office; both directions are tested.
(3) SetupPackageReader.Open(path|stream, password, expectations, TimeProvider) and the non-throwing Inspect(...) both exist. SetupExpectations carries exactly PinnedOrgSigningPub / InstalledDeviceId / InstalledExportSeq (plus MaxFutureSkew and StagingDirectory). SetupCheckResult is a per-item list with Ok/Failed/Absent and an ErrorCode, in enum = display order, with no Arabic anywhere in src/Wakeel.Crypto (grepped: zero files contain Arabic script). All ten specified items are present; the extra leading Package item is where the file-wide verdicts live and is a sensible addition, not a deviation. Every specified rejection maps to the specified code: invalid signature -> Signature/BadSignature; wrong password -> Package/WrongPassword; device.id mismatch -> Device/OtherDevice; exportSeq below installed -> Package/Older; exportedAt more than the skew ahead -> Package/FutureDate; org key different from the pinned key -> Organisation/Tampered; unreadable setup.json -> Package/Corrupt.
(4) PackagePassword.New gives 16 Crockford characters from RandomBytes.NextInt32 (80 bits, no modulo bias). Display groups 4-4-4-4; Normalize folds case, the separators and O/I/L; both sides derive from the normalised form, and the writer insists on a well-formed password so the file's strength is a property of the format.
(5) Every listed test exists and asserts real behaviour, not tautologies: both round trips, wrong password, tampered payload, tampered manifest (re-signed where the point is to bypass the signature and hit a later rule), other device, older exportSeq, future date both at container level and description-only level, pinned-key mismatch, revocation carried through and verified, and determinism across two writes with the same clock. The determinism test is the good kind - it asserts that Producer, CreatedAt, Type, Version, Mode and Entries are equal AND that the Argon2 salt and the payload bytes differ.
(6) The three B0-closeout lows are all done and each is pinned: ContainerTests now asserts ExtractTo also throws Tampered on the oversized entry; PairingTests has a [Theory] with one case per plain field (orgId/officeId/pcDeviceId) built over a genuinely valid computer signature, and a second [Theory] with the three key-half combinations; ContainerEntrySource derives SegmentInvalidChars from Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars() minus the two separators, pinned by Every_character_the_platform_refuses_in_a_file_name_is_refused_in_an_entry_name which walks the platform list.

SECURITY - what I checked and what holds. VERIFY BEFORE DECRYPT: ContainerReader.Open parses the manifest, validates its shape, hashes the payload and verifies the Ed25519 signature over DomainSeparation('wakeel.container') || SHA256(manifest) || SHA256(payload) before returning; Inspect then checks Kind == Org and runs the chain; only then is ContainerKeySource.FromPassword used and setup.json decrypted. No payload byte is touched on any failure path. TOFU PINNING: orgSigningKey = expectations.PinnedOrgSigningPub ?? producer.SigningPublicKey, and CheckOrganisation afterwards insists that setup.json's org.id and org.x25519Pub equal the root certificate's and that org.signingPub decodes to exactly the key the chain was checked with - so the key the installation goes on to pin is provably the key that verified the file, and on a pinned machine a foreign root is refused at Organisation/Tampered before anything else is believed. An_organisation_section_that_disagrees_with_the_signing_certificate_is_refused is the test that makes this real. SECRETS: deviceSeed and officeKey appear only inside setup.json, which lives only inside the AEAD payload; nothing in ContainerManifest carries them (the manifest holds only name, size and the plaintext SHA-256, and both secrets are high-entropy so that hash is not a confirmation oracle). No Setup container carries an adminSealedKey, correctly, since ContainerKinds.RequiresAdminCopy excludes Setup and the organisation already holds everything in the file. PRIMITIVES: no invented cryptography; Ed25519 via NSec, AES-256-GCM framed, Argon2id via Konscious, HKDF-SHA256, all with domain separation labels. The Argon2 ceiling added to Argon2Params.Validate is a genuine hardening for exactly this format - the cost parameters ride in a manifest the machine has not trusted yet - and it is a pure tightening: AutoTune never exceeds 64 MB / 3 / 2, so no artefact this product has ever written falls outside the new 1 GB / 16 / 16 window. NULL-SAFETY AGAINST A HOSTILE DOCUMENT: SetupContent.Parse settles the shape of every non-nullable member, and every later check re-guards certificate.Body, unit elements and revocation entries, so a truncated or crafted setup.json leaves this project as a CryptoException and never as a NullReferenceException.

EXTRA HARDENING I VERIFIED AS REAL, NOT DECORATIVE. The seeds must be the private half of the certified keys (CheckSeeds imports them and compares both public halves) - without it an installation could activate from a file whose certificate it can never use. A revocation list that is not properly signed by the organisation fails its own item and is deliberately NOT passed to the device check, so a forged list cannot be used to lock a device out; both halves of that are asserted. A setup file may carry only the four known entry names, which stops a wholesale ExtractTo from dropping attacker-chosen files into the installation folder on a first run when there is no pin yet. A pinned key of the wrong length is a hard CryptoException rather than a silent fall-back to first-run trust - that one is the difference between a bug and a downgrade attack, and it has its own test. Unlisted entries inside the inner zip are never extracted, because both ReadOne and ExtractTo iterate Manifest.Entries only. The FileStream is closed on every failure path of Inspect, and ContainerReader never takes the stream over until it has an archive, so there is no double dispose.

WRITER/READER SYMMETRY. SetupPackageWriter.Verify runs the reader's own SetupChecker over the content before signing, with SetupExpectations.FirstRun and the export clock, so the administration tool cannot hand a person a file the agent would refuse; The_writer_refuses_to_sign_a_description_it_would_itself_reject covers a future date, seeds that do not match the certificate, a short office key, an employee number out of range and an office that is not in the structure. A badly signed revocation list is also caught there, via FirstFailure, even though Revocation is not a required item. The root certificate is issued at content.ExportedAt rather than from the clock, which is what makes two exports of one description byte-identical.

API USABILITY. The writer takes exactly what A05/A09 will have (content, three optional stream factories, password, org identity, path or stream, clock) and returns the ContainerManifest. The reader gives W02 and W03 what they need: Inspect never throws for anything the screen must display, the check list is already in display order, each line is (Item, Status, ErrorCode?) with the Arabic owned entirely by the interface layer, and the activation button goes through Require(). SetupPackage exposes Content, Checks, Manifest, Producer, Has/Read/TryRead, the three named optional readers and ExtractTo. The two things B1 must be told: set StagingDirectory (finding 2) and do not read entries out of a package whose checks failed (finding 1).

VERDICT: accept. Build and tests are green with warnings as errors, every specification item including the three closeout findings is implemented and pinned by a test that would fail if the code were reverted, and the trust model - verify before decrypt, trust on first sight then pin, pinned key wins thereafter, root signs setup files and nothing else - is correct in the order the code performs it. All eight findings are low: two are documentation reconciliations for the supervisor (the org-root decision and the director/manager split), five are hardening or ergonomics suggestions for this package, and one is a pre-existing container-reader note I record rather than charge to this work.
